specs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a separate landscape 3:2 visual concept mockup for the existing 2D pixel-art game Midnight Maki. This is one cohesive game environment, not an asset sheet, collage, brochure or isometric diorama. Inputs: Image 1 is the actual current restaurant screenshot, use it for Japanese identity and recognizable architecture but eliminate the huge empty dark margins; Image 2 is the actual cast reference, preserve the recognizable protagonist Sofi with dark brown hair and pink clothing plus the three raccoons Pip (gray large), Spicy (gray red headband chef) and Rigg (brown); Image 3 is the selected asset combination reference, use its actual furniture shapes, colors and pixel density as the intended environment vocabulary. Create an honest, practical near-gameplay mockup rather than ornate illustration. Orthographic top-down three-quarter RPG camera like the screenshot, clean raster pixel art, discrete square pixels, hard edges, no anti-aliased painted illustration, no 3D or isometric angles. Composition consistent across alternatives: a wide rectangular Japanese sushi restaurant occupying the upper 75% of the frame, a thin outdoor garden walkway with three tiny vegetable beds along the bottom 25%, roof removed for visibility. Rear wall with MIDNIGHT MAKI sign and two red lanterns; sushi counter and prep kitchen along the back wall; 3 small dining tables in lower center; entrance bottom center; Sofi serving at center; all three raccoons around counter at left. Same room layout and object/character counts for fair comparison. Camera framed tightly on the world, no empty margins, no phone frame, no oversized UI. Subtle dusk outside and warm interior illumination, retain legibility. Only readable world text is "MIDNIGHT MAKI" on its wooden sign. No extra character cast. Do not copy the labels or contact sheet layout from image 3. Prioritize plausible achievable tile-based visuals.
VARIANT A — evolution of the existing identity. Use the Bitglow kitchen/living-room furniture in reference 3: medium walnut and honey wood cabinetry, cream worktops, modest domestic kitchen details, cohesive furniture proportions, sage green accents. Keep the Japanese counter, lanterns and wood slat interior from the actual game. Furniture has clear small pixel outlines and moderate detailing. Garden has three low warm-outline Cozy Farm Lite vegetable beds, carrot and tomato. Small sushi icons represented as very small 16px-looking food on counter and plates, never giant illustrations. This should read as a tasteful practical improvement of the existing game, not a total reskin. No beds or bathroom fixtures in the restaurant, reference those only as palette.

VARIANT B — rustic cabin interpretation using Cosy Cabin Simple and Pixel Tales nature, as visible in reference 3. Preserve the Japanese sushi purpose and original cast. Use the sushi pack's long wooden trays, sake cups and chopsticks in readable scale on the counter and tables. Outdoor strip has a more textured earth path, leafy Pixel Tales vegetation and small crop plots. Cozy and intimate, rustic brown palette; this is still a working sushi restaurant, not a medieval tavern. No swords, fireplaces, beds or fantasy decor.

Use the small coherent simple cabinets/chairs and domestic floor shapes seen in reference 3. Keep the Japanese identity, the same three dining tables/counter positions and same recognizable original cast, adapt their rendering only slightly to the simpler environment.
